findings.description: No canonical marketplace event taxonomy exists.
Behavioral events and transactional facts are not governed by one semantic authority map.
Cross-domain anonymous/authenticated identity stitching is undefined.
Current deduplication protects replay but not fabricated visitor/session identities.
Behavioral sources use incompatible timestamp authorities.
No canonical lateness, watermark or finalized-window contract exists.
Current live aggregate views expose no immutable metric revision or source fingerprint.
No cross-domain analytics reconciliation authority exists.
GMV, take rate and revenue cannot be production-authoritative while PAY remains contract_only.
Retention, deletion, anonymization and persistent anonymous identity depend on LEGAL-B03.
Metric ownership, quality thresholds and business-alert semantics are not canonical.

mandatoryInvariants: browser-generated visitor/session IDs never become human identity authority
client event IDs are idempotency hints and not proof of occurrence
behavioral events transactional facts and operational observability remain distinct
transactional outcomes are sourced from owning domains
order transaction facts are projected from ORD
payment outcomes remain unavailable until PAY has external authority
authenticated actor identity is resolved server-side
canonical subject dimensions are resolved from server authorities
server receipt time is never client-controlled
client timestamps are advisory unless a versioned policy says otherwise
semantic deduplication is separate from transport idempotency
anonymous to authenticated stitching remains disabled until privacy policy approval
cross-device anonymous stitching is disabled
analytics payloads minimize personal and payment data
metric definitions are versioned
historical metric snapshots are reproducible
same source definition and window produce the same fingerprint
finalized metric history is never silently overwritten
historical corrections create explicit revisions
reconciliation never edits a canonical source to make analytics agree
source-domain defects are owned by the source domain
missing authority returns unavailable rather than synthetic zero
data-quality alerts and business-performance signals are separate
every canonical metric declares source and projection ownership
fixtures browser caches and synthetic staging data never become production authority
